# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook

## Threshold point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says clauses marked [STANDARD] have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **I have disregarded this.**

- It is the counterparty's own characterisation, not an agreed position.
- Nothing in our playbook records any such acceptance.
- Almost every [STANDARD] item departs from our positions.

Every clause has been reviewed on its merits. The deal team should say in the cover email to the mark-up that the Buyer has not accepted any limitation or disclosure package and that the labels have no effect.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Clause 12.1 caps general Warranty Claims at 20% (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000). The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. No such authority has been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The Seller has opened at our unauthorised fallback, and we cannot concede it without Amelia Frost's written approval.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** Clause 12.2 sets a de minimis of AUD 25,000 and a basket of AUD 250,000, with only the excess over the basket recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** A de minimis of AUD 5,000 and a basket of AUD 50,000, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery.** The Seller's figures are five times ours, and an excess-only basket would permanently wipe out AUD 250,000 of valid claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** Clause 12.3/13 requires notice within 18 months. It also says any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. The 18-month figure is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insist on 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" language.** 18 months is unauthorised, and the default-application wording quietly extends the general time bar to Fundamental, Tax, fraud and indemnity claims (see SPA-N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would sit under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** Title and capacity are the core of what we are paying AUD 24m for, so capping them at 20% and 18 months is unacceptable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** There is no fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature." Read literally, that would cover fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out that overrides everything else.** This is non-waivable under the playbook, and no one on the deal team has authority to concede it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter paras 1.1 and 1.2 generally disclose the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records. Para 1.4 adds a broad non-admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, with no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or prudent searches.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject paras 1.1 and 1.2.** Limit disclosure to the specific items in paras 2 to 10, each fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope. General disclosure would empty the warranties of content.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars any claim for matters known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier must refer to named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete clause 8.3.** The adviser and "discoverable" limbs would turn our own due diligence into a defence for the Seller.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Clause 3/6.3 commits to reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered. Disclosure para 2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are not acceptable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Make it a hard condition precedent requiring:
  - an effective Bluefen consent;
  - evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied;
  - stronger Seller obligations (at least all reasonable endeavours), with a Buyer walk-right.

  Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m and roughly 30% of revenue, so a consent with unsatisfied conditions puts the main customer at risk.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Clause 2/7 deals with the facility (about AUD 3.2m outstanding) through a release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure para 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Require a payout letter dated close to Completion, payment straight to Riverlark in the funds flow, and executed releases and discharges (including PPSR) at Completion. This fits the debt-free/cash-free basis and avoids unsecured reliance on the Seller after Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The funds flow note says the DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. Disclosure para 5 confirms they are missing from the funds flow and says nothing about on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, either as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Add a specific line item or deduction for the bonuses and on-costs, backed by a specific indemnity. The obligations sit with the Company, so leaving them out of the funds flow shifts the cost to the Buyer without saying so.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Clause 11.1 limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering:
  - IP ownership and transfer failure;
  - third-party claims;
  - the cost of remediation and re-development.

  It must preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment under DD-004 cl. 7.3.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow form.** Broaden the indemnity and require evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment at or before Completion. The AUD 180,000 open amount in DD-010 is unverified either way, and paying it alone does not prove that IP has transferred.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** Clause 4.6/Schedule 6 calls this a "preliminary operational matter" that is "not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** Preserved logs, a continuing investigation and regular updates. We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation, and do not overstate the incident either.** Add covenants to:
  - preserve logs and evidence;
  - complete the investigation, including whether any eligible data breach assessment is needed;
  - give the Buyer prompt updates and consultation rights before any notification.

  Also exclude the matter from general disclosure and the knowledge bar. Neither side can yet say what the outcome is.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Treats the three renewals (AUD 330,000 in total) as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of the renewals, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reserve the position; do not accept or reject the label yet.** Ask for the contracts, the timing, termination rights and accrual status (Disclosure para 8 is silent on these). Then decide whether a warranty, Debt-like item or covenant is appropriate. The facts are not yet known.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Clauses 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, together with the Tax/IP and Title statements, fold every category into the general regime by default.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/indemnity and covenant claims each kept in their own regime, with no hidden override by the general limitations.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Add an express hierarchy clause stating that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, and delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" wording. As drafted, the default rule erodes every specially negotiated protection.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Relies on the DD-012 share register as evidence of 100% title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller and is not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** Require:
  - ASIC searches reconciled to the register;
  - share certificates;
  - the share issue and transfer history;
  - a PPSR search with releases;
  - board and shareholder authority.

  Back this with uncapped Fundamental warranties (SPA-N-004). Disclosure para 10 itself concedes the register is not verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Says the Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain **OPEN**. Assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation and record Tax/IP as open.** Keep negotiating standalone Tax and IP regimes, including a tax indemnity and appropriate periods. We have not agreed them, so they cannot be treated as resolved under the general regime.

---

## Summary

| Item | Position |
|---|---|
| 001 Cap | Reject; 25% / AUD 6.0m (no authority for 20%) |
| 002 Thresholds | Reject; AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar |
| 003 Time limit | Reject; 24 months (no authority for 18) |
| 004 Fundamental/Title | Reject; 100% cap, 6+ years, outside general limits |
| 005 Fraud | Reject; mandatory full carve-out (non-waivable) |
| 006 Disclosure | Reject general disclosure; specific fair disclosure only |
| 007 Buyer knowledge | Delete cl. 8.3 |
| 008 Bluefen | Reject; effective consent plus conditions evidence as CP |
| 009 Riverlark | Reject; payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion |
| 010 Bonuses | Reject; line item or Seller-funded, including on-costs |
| 011 Ironquay | Reject narrow form; broaden, keep SOW3 cure |
| 012 DD-006 | Covenants for preservation, investigation and updates; no conclusions either way |
| 013 Sandbar | Reserve; diligence first, no automatic Debt treatment |
| 014 Categories | Reject; express hierarchy clause |
| 015 Title | Reject DD-012 alone; independent evidence |
| 016 Tax/IP | Record as OPEN, not settled |

**Escalation:** None of these recommendations uses a playbook fallback. If the team wants to move on the cap (SPA-N-001) or the time limit (SPA-N-003), it needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft before any counter-offer goes out.

- **Recommendation:** **Reserve the position; do not accept or reject the label yet.** Ask for the contracts, the timing, termination rights and accrual status (Disclosure para 8 is silent on these). Then decide whether a warranty, Debt-like item or covenant is appropriate. The facts are not yet known.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Clauses 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, together with the Tax/IP and Title statements, fold every category into the general regime by default.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/indemnity and covenant claims each kept in their own regime, with no hidden override by the general limitations.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Add an express hierarchy clause stating that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, and delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" wording. As drafted, the default rule erodes every specially negotiated protection.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Relies on the DD-012 share register as evidence of 100% title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller and is not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** Require:
  - ASIC searches reconciled to the register;
  - share certificates;
  - the share issue and transfer history;
  - a PPSR search with releases;
  - board and shareholder authority.

  Back this with uncapped Fundamental warranties (SPA-N-004). Disclosure para 10 itself concedes the register is not verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Says the Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain **OPEN**. Assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation and record Tax/IP as open.** Keep negotiating standalone Tax and IP regimes, including a tax indemnity and appropriate periods. We have not agreed them, so they cannot be treated as resolved under the general regime.
